name: Trichuris trichiura

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Egg: typically about 50–55 × 20–25 µm, brown barrel or lemon shape with thick smooth shell and clear plugs at both poles; broader measurement ranges occur.
Adults have a thin anterior portion embedded in colonic mucosa and a thicker posterior portion.

transmission.detail: Eggs passed in stool embryonate in soil; ingestion leads to development and adult residence in the large intestine.

life_cycle.detail: A host swallows infective eggs from contaminated hands or food.
Larvae hatch in the small intestine; adults establish in the colon.

distribution: Tropical and subtropical regions, including Thailand, especially where sanitation is limited.
clinical_significance: Heavy infection can cause chronic diarrhea, anemia, impaired growth and rectal prolapse.
diagnostics: Stool wet mount or quantitative egg microscopy; 400× resolves plug and shell detail.
differential_diagnosis: Capillaria philippinensis eggs are generally smaller, striated and have less prominent plugs; verify calibrated size.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
